newsitem.title: DENMARK: BG Bank H1 97 core earnings up 31 pct.
newsitem.headline: BG Bank H1 97 core earnings up 31 pct.

text.p: Denmark's third biggest bank, BG Bank, said on Tuesday its first-half 1997 core earnings had risen 31 percent compared to the same 1996 period, fuelled by impressive net interest and fees income and dramatically lower losses and bad debt provisions.
Operating profits for this year's first six months were 988.9 million crowns against 753.7 million crowns a year ago, the bank said in a statement with its 1997 interim results.
It said net interest and fees earnings, some five percent up on 1996's first-half at 3.194 billion crowns, helped core earnings although these were partly offset by 3.6 percent higher costs.

BG Bank's first-half 1997 result, the first to be announced by one of Denmark's big three banks, showed an almost 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 1.063 billion crowns compared to 1996's interim 821 million crowns.

A steep fall in losses and bad debt provisions for the period to 175 million crowns from 297 million crowns a year ago was also seen as a factor contributing to BG Bank's improved first-half result, which was above analysts' expectations.
At 1130 GMT, the BG Bank share traded at 395 crowns, six crowns up from the start but unchanged since the announcement of its interim results.
